title: Alpha gate, FX and meta-labeling
hypothesis: An FX sleeve diversifies the book, and a meta-label model improves trend entries.
question: We built a reusable alpha gate, then asked two questions: does an FX trend sleeve help, and can a small classifier decide which trend signals to take (meta-labeling)?
prior: Meta-labeling (López de Prado 2018) sizes or vetoes an existing signal rather than predicting prices, which suits a low signal-to-noise setting.
citations: López de Prado, M. (2018). Advances in Financial Machine Learning. Wiley.
Bailey, D., Borwein, J., López de Prado, M. & Zhu, Q. (2017). The Probability of Backtest Overfitting. J. Computational Finance 20(4).
method: Alpha gate: economic prior; net Sharpe > 0.40 and improves the book; Deflated Sharpe and PBO; block-bootstrap, plateau, crisis and correlation checks.
Meta model = XGBoost on per-asset trend entries, triple-barrier labels, purged K-fold.
Model-capacity sweep (depth 2/4/8) plus uniqueness weights, bagging and calibration.
verdict_reason: Signal-level meta-labeling passed (book Sharpe 1.04 → 1.21 at OOS AUC 0.52) and the small model beat bigger ones. FX trend failed (Sharpe 0.15, Deflated Sharpe ≈ 0) and lowered the blend. Book-level meta-labeling had no skill (AUC 0.507).
lessons: The signal sits near an information ceiling (AUC ~0.52–0.54); bigger models overfit.
footer: Research code is private; methods summarised below.
